data.text/markdown:
This simple model shows that even a small preference for neighbors of similar race can lead to high levels of segregation.

Set Up

Suppose we have two types of people: orange people and green people. we will assume there are 250 of each type. These agents all live on a single unit square. The location of an agent is just a point $ (x, y) $, where $ 0 < x < 1 $ and $ 0 < y < 1 $.

Preferences

An agent is happy if M (Minimum) of her N nearest neighbors are of the same type as her. Otherwise, she is unhappy. Nearest = 'Euclidean distance' in the unit square.

Initialization

These 500 agents are initially randomly mixed together: each agent independently and randomly draws a location from a bivariate uniform distribution S = (0,1) x (0,1).

data.text/markdown:
How the model works

At each round (time period), each agent can either stay or move to a random location in the unit square. An agent stays if the agent is happy. The algorith for moving is as follows:
  1. Draw a random location in $ S $
  2. If happy at new location, move there
  3. Else, go to step 1
We cycle through all agents in one round, in a fixed order. We continue to cycle until no one wishes to move.

data.text/markdown: What is striking about the pictures is how rapidly racial integration breaks down. This is despite the fact that people in the model don’t actually mind living mixed with the other type. Even with these preferences, the outcome is a high degree of segregation.

Watch agents move one by one

This walkthrough uses the orange and green simulation above. Each row is one complete round, starting from the positions at the end of the previous round. Agents are visited in order: all 250 orange agents, then all 250 green agents. Move the orange slider first. Once it reaches 250, the green slider advances through the green agents. The buttons beside either slider move one agent at a time. A ring marks the last agent visited, and an arrow shows its move, if it moved. A flat step means that agent was already happy and stayed put.

This section has its own nearest neighbor count ||(N||), minimum same-type count ||(M||), and random seed. Each type has a distinct color. The slider again shows the initial state and every later round, including unchanged rounds after equilibrium.
